synopsis: CAN or J1939 is a source for recording machine state at adequate rate and precision, covering motion, braking, propulsion, automation, engine state and payload, plus implement positions where relevant [f5634]. Recorded CAN or J1939 traffic can also be used for hardware-in-the-loop data injection alongside camera RAW-data and radar detection-level injection [f5281]. Changes to CAN or J1939 interfaces without impact analysis are identified as early warnings that prototype changes may invalidate the pre-built simulator; one account specifies the second quarter of 2027, while another refers to 2027 generally [f10761, f11028]. The recording requirement does not specify numerical rate or precision thresholds, and the injection method does not establish that recorded traffic alone provides adequate coverage [f5634, f5281].

relations.note: Both flag unassessed CAN/J1939 interface changes as warnings of prototype–simulator mismatch.
Machine-state recording supplies CAN/J1939 traffic that can be reused for HIL injection.
CAN/J1939 injection fidelity depends on assessing prototype interface changes.
